blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Infectious Diseases Society for Obstetrics and Gynecology (Pidsog) is pushing three policy measures to improve access to maternal care, including the inclusion of recommended vaccines in Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth’s) antenatal care package. The group plans to develop a policy brief seeking the inclusion of tetanus, diphtheria and pertussis (Tdap) and, pending evidence review, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines in the PhilHealth antenatal care benefit package.
